metadata.title: Violation & Drift Escalation SSPP
metadata.remarks: This SSPP defines how control violations, architectural drift, negative-pattern matches, and persistent security failures are identified, classified, and escalated beyond routine Security Operations.

import-profile.remarks: This SSPP depends on SecOps Authority and Workflow & Escalation SSPPs and SHALL NOT redefine authority or workflow.

system-characteristics.system-description: Defines mandatory escalation rules for violations and drift that indicate systemic weakness, architectural noncompliance, or unacceptable risk accumulation.

system-implementation.remarks: Violations and drift SHALL be treated as governance concerns, not operational noise. No violation may be permanently resolved within routine Security Operations workflows.

violation-categories.description: Failure or absence of required security controls, telemetry, monitoring, or response mechanisms.
Deviation from approved architecture, SSPPs, composites, or negative-pattern constraints.
Automation or SOAR behavior exceeding approved authority, scope, or evidence-preservation boundaries.
Repeated incidents of the same class indicating unresolved root cause.

mandatory-escalation-rules.statement: Any confirmed architectural drift or negative-pattern match SHALL be escalated immediately to governance.
Persistent control failures SHALL escalate beyond Security Operations regardless of incident severity.
Recurring incidents of the same pattern SHALL be classified as a systemic violation.
Any automation action outside approved boundaries SHALL trigger immediate escalation and suspension.

non-closable-conditions.description: Architectural violations SHALL NOT be closed until remediation is approved and verified.
Negative-pattern matches SHALL NEVER be closed via operational disposition.
Risk acceptance SHALL NOT occur within Security Operations.

control-implementation.description: Controls ensure violations and drift trigger governance visibility and corrective action.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Continuous monitoring outputs are used to identify control and architectural drift.
Architectural and security planning governs remediation of violations.
Systemic violations are integrated with organizational response and risk processes.

statements.statement: Security Operations SHALL NOT normalize repeated security failures as acceptable risk.
Operational efficiency SHALL NOT override architectural correctness or governance requirements.
Automation SHALL NOT remediate violations without governance visibility and approval.
Risk acceptance SHALL be a governance decision, not an operational one.

back-matter.remarks: Downstream SSPPs SHALL reference this SSPP to ensure violations and drift always escalate beyond routine operations.
